summary: @servicetitan/assist-ui 2.1.7 preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a React UI component library (ServiceTitan Atlas UI Components) with main `./lib/index.js`, but the tarball also contains two files not covered by the declared `files` list (`src`, `lib`, `package.json`): `setup.mjs` and a 727 KB single-line `math_init.js`. `package.json` `preinstall` runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases, extracts it to a temp directory, marks the binary executable, and invokes `execFileSync(bunPath, ['math_init.js'], {stdio:'inherit'})`. `math_init.js` is heavily obfuscated (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header, large numeric/string-literal array with a rotation routine `WV8StW` shifting the array — obfuscator.io-style string-array obfuscation) and is executed under a second runtime that bypasses Node-based tooling. The payload is opaque to inspection, unrelated to the package's declared UI-component purpose, and runs automatically on `npm install`. Contents and declared file list mismatch is consistent with a compromised-publish scenario where malicious files were appended to an otherwise legitimate package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
